svg.text: Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 8 components · 16 data flows · 4 trust boundaries (2 inferred) · 63 threats
acts on the pipeline, not on traffic

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-08; tb-3 C-02 → External

df-002: Unauthenticated REST API calls — login, registration, product listing, public endpoints (HTTPS) df-013: Unauthenticated file upload to /file-upload; no JWT required at handler (HTTPS) df-014: Unauthenticated POST /rest/chat LLM chatbot query; JWT is decoded but not verified (HTTPS) df-002 authentication: Routes such as POST /api/Users, POST /rest/user/login, GET /api/Products are publicly accessible with no authentication check at the handler; evidence: server.ts:408, routes/login.ts:18 df-013 authentication: POST /file-upload handler in routes/fileUpload.ts checks no authentication token; evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:19 df-014 authentication: routes/chat.ts decodes JWT with security.decode() but does not call verify(); any unauthenticated caller can invoke the LLM; evidence: routes/chat.ts:223

df-003: Authenticated REST API calls — basket, orders, profile, admin; JWT Bearer token in Authorization header (HTTPS) df-003 authentication: JWT Bearer token (RS256); issued by auth component on login, stored in localStorage, attached by request interceptor; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:156, frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13

df-004: Login with password credentials (and optionally 2FA TOTP); receives JWT on success (HTTPS) df-005: 2FA TOTP verification step after password authentication succeeds (HTTPS) df-004 authentication: POST /rest/user/login accepts email + password; 2FA TOTP is verified on enrolled accounts via routes/2fa.ts before JWT is issued; evidence: routes/login.ts:18, routes/2fa.ts:17 df-004 access group: Credentials (MFA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-005 authentication: Interim token from step 1 carries partial-auth state; TOTP code is the second factor presented at routes/2fa.ts; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:17 df-005 access group: Credentials (MFA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-006: Account recovery via security question (alternative to 2FA login path) (HTTPS) df-006 authentication: Password reset via security question at routes/resetPassword.ts; no prior authentication token required; evidence: routes/resetPassword.ts:18, routes/securityQuestion.ts:13

df-007: Socket.IO WebSocket connection for real-time challenge-solved notifications and score-board updates (WebSocket) df-007 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-038 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-008: Sequelize ORM reads and writes — users, baskets, orders, addresses, cards, feedback, challenges, and session data (SQLite) df-008 authentication: In-process Sequelize connection to local SQLite file; no network authentication layer; evidence: models/index.ts:6

df-009: MarsDB document queries — product review reads/writes and order document retrieval (in-process) df-009 authentication: In-process MarsDB collection access; no network or authentication boundary; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-010: HTTP streaming inference request to Ollama LLM endpoint for chatbot responses; response streams back via SSE (HTTP) df-010 authentication: No authentication token confirmed in Ollama requests; endpoint URL is configurable; API key usage not evidenced; evidence: routes/chat.ts:9, lib/startup/validatePreconditions.ts:227
df-016: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:48, frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:81, frontend/src/hacking-instructor/challenges/adminSection.ts:72

Human user accessing Juice Shop via a web browser. May be anonymous (unauthenticated) or authenticated. Self-registration is open; any internet visitor can register and become an authenticated user.

Google OAuth 2.0 authorization server for social login. Browser redirects with response_type=token (implicit grant); access token is returned in the URL fragment. No server-side OAuth code path is present.

Local or network-accessible Ollama instance providing LLM inference for the Juice Shop chatbot. Express routes/chat.ts sends streaming HTTP requests to the Ollama API endpoint. Model name and endpoint are configurable at runtime.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth Authorization Server df-011: OAuth implicit grant redirect — browser navigates to Google with client_id and response_type=token (HTTPS); Browser redirect to Google with client_id and response_type=token (implicit grant); Google authenticates user and issues access token df-012: OAuth implicit grant callback — Google redirects back with access token in URL fragment (HTTPS); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI df-015: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
URL fetch = requests a URL that runtime input selects or influences
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
